sources.title: Earth
sources.usage_note: Public NASA reference page; individual facts identify their supporting section.

sources.title: Mars: Facts
sources.usage_note: Public NASA reference page; individual facts identify their supporting section. The publication page declares this update date in its structured metadata.

sources.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, National Space Science Data Center
sources.title: Mars Fact Sheet
sources.usage_note: NASA reference table of Martian atmosphere composition, mean-reference surface pressure, and temperature values. Atmospheric pressure varies with location and season.

sources.title: NASA's MAVEN Reveals Most of Mars' Atmosphere Was Lost to Space
sources.usage_note: NASA MAVEN atmospheric-escape release. It attributes most long-term Martian atmospheric loss to solar wind and radiation, including sputtering.

sources.title: 1,000 Days in Orbit: MAVEN's Top 10 Discoveries at Mars
sources.usage_note: NASA MAVEN overview documenting diffuse and proton aurora at Mars and localized magnetized crust in the absence of a present global magnetic field.

sources.publisher: NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node
sources.title: Mars Global Surveyor MOLA MEGDR v2.0
sources.usage_note: MOLA global topography grid label. Elevations are relative to the MOLA areoid; the 128-pixel-per-degree grid is a binned/interpolated product.

sources.title: The bulk composition of Mars
sources.usage_note: Peer-reviewed reconstructed whole-planet bulk-composition model. Values are model estimates, not direct global surface measurements.

sources.title: Evidence for a liquid silicate layer atop the Martian core
sources.usage_note: InSight seismic reanalysis giving a model-dependent liquid-core radius and an overlying molten silicate layer.

sources.title: NASA's InSight Reveals the Deep Interior of Mars
sources.usage_note: NASA/JPL overview of InSight interior inferences, including model-dependent crust depth and Mars's single-plate crust.

sources.title: Mars Relay Network
sources.usage_note: NASA/ESA Mars relay-network status page. Its Feb-May 2026 data table is a scoped relay-network snapshot, not a complete Mars-orbit object catalog.

sources.title: NASA Says Farewell to MAVEN Mars Mission
sources.usage_note: NASA announcement that MAVEN's mission ended and the spacecraft was not recoverable. It is not an orbit determination or general Mars-object catalog.

sources.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Solar System Dynamics
sources.title: Horizons: SpaceX Roadster (spacecraft), -143205
sources.usage_note: JPL Horizons identifies the SpaceX Roadster and its Sun-centered orbital elements and lists predicted Mars close approaches. It does not place the object in Mars orbit.

sources.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Solar System Dynamics
sources.title: Planetary Physical Parameters
sources.usage_note: NASA JPL table of selected planetary physical characteristics; use its stated parameter definitions and Earth-row values.

sources.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Solar System Dynamics
sources.title: Approximate Positions of the Planets
sources.usage_note: JPL-published J2000 Keplerian elements and rates for the listed planets. The Earth entries describe the Earth-Moon barycenter; Mars entries describe Mars. Values are valid from 1800 through 2050.

sources.title: Satellite Catalog: Latest Orbital Statistics for Earth Orbit
sources.usage_note: Public SATCAT statistics snapshot. CelesTrak reports its source-data currency and distinguishes 18 SDS GP data from supplemental and analyst catalogs. Values must be refreshed as a dated snapshot.

sources.title: Earth's Magnetosphere
sources.usage_note: NASA explanatory article on the magnetosphere's interaction with solar material and its role in atmospheric retention.

sources.title: Trends in Globally Averaged CO2
sources.usage_note: Globally averaged marine-surface monthly mean CO2 record. Recent values are provisional and may be recalibrated by NOAA.

sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.title: Global Forest Resources Assessment 2020
sources.usage_note: Global forest assessment across 236 countries and territories for 1990-2020. Forest extent and change rates are assessment estimates, not real-time observations.

sources.title: Trends in Globally Averaged CH4
sources.usage_note: Globally averaged marine-surface monthly mean methane record. Recent values are provisional and may be recalibrated by NOAA.

sources.title: Trends in Globally Averaged N2O
sources.usage_note: Globally averaged marine-surface monthly mean nitrous-oxide record. Recent values are provisional and may be recalibrated by NOAA.

sources.title: Primary Production of the Biosphere: Integrating Terrestrial and Oceanic Components
sources.usage_note: Satellite-model global net primary production estimate. This historical benchmark is not a current annual satellite-product aggregation.

sources.publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
sources.title: World Population Prospects 2024
sources.usage_note: Official UN global population estimates and projections. The displayed value is a rounded 2025 world estimate from the 2024 revision.

sources.title: Catalogue of Life Annual Release 2026
sources.usage_note: Current Catalogue of Life release. The catalogue notes that its coverage is incomplete and may contain errors.

sources.title: How Many Species Are There on Earth and in the Ocean?
sources.usage_note: Peer-reviewed model-based estimate of global eukaryotic species richness; it is an estimate with stated uncertainty, not a current inventory.

sources.title: Homo sapiens (human), Taxonomy ID 9606
sources.usage_note: Curated taxonomy record identifying Homo sapiens within Eukaryota and Metazoa.

sources.title: Biology 2e: The Chemical Foundation of Life
sources.usage_note: Open biology textbook describing carbon as the foundation of Earth's organic biomolecules.

sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.title: World Ocean Atlas
sources.usage_note: Global ocean-temperature climatology. The displayed surface temperature is an annual climatological reference, not a live satellite retrieval.

sources.publisher: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies
sources.title: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis version 4: Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index
sources.usage_note: Monthly global land-ocean temperature change relative to the 1951-1980 baseline; incorporates GHCN v4 land stations and ERSST v5 ocean areas.

sources.title: Records of Weather and Climate Extremes Table
sources.usage_note: WMO archive of formally evaluated weather and climate records. Values are station observations of near-surface air temperature, not land or ocean skin temperature.

sources.publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center
sources.title: Arctic zigs; Antarctic zags
sources.usage_note: NSIDC monthly Arctic sea-ice extent analysis derived from the NOAA Sea Ice Index. This is a time-specific satellite-era observation, not a global annual mean.

sources.title: Ice Sheets - Earth Indicator
sources.usage_note: GRACE and GRACE Follow-On satellite measurements of Greenland and Antarctic ice-sheet mass variation.

sources.title: How Much Water is There on Earth?
sources.usage_note: Global water inventory estimate. Atmospheric water volume is an approximate inventory, not a real-time observation.

sources.title: How deep is the ocean?
sources.usage_note: NOAA reference for global ocean depth and the deepest documented ocean location. Its companion elevation reference provides the highest elevation above mean sea level.

sources.title: Compositional Model for the Earth's Core
sources.usage_note: Bulk-Earth elemental mass-fraction model derived from cosmochemical and geochemical constraints. It includes the core, mantle, and crust; it is not a direct global measurement.

sources.title: The Carbon Cycle
sources.usage_note: Reference carbon reservoir estimates. Reservoir magnitudes are historical, approximate inventories expressed as gigatonnes of carbon, not current annual measurements.

sources.publisher: Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors
sources.title: Global map of solid Earth surface heat flow
sources.usage_note: Global conductive heat-flow compilation. The reported 47 TW is a model-derived estimate of total surface heat loss.

sources.title: Geophysical and geochemical constraints on geoneutrino fluxes from Earth's mantle
sources.usage_note: Earth radiogenic-power estimate constrained by geochemical and geophysical models. The display rounds the model estimate to 20 TW.

sources.title: Earthquake Facts and Statistics
sources.usage_note: USGS estimated worldwide annual frequency by magnitude class. The displayed daily rate is derived from the estimated 500,000 annual earthquakes of magnitude 2.5-5.4.

sources.title: The Cosmic Connection: An Extraterrestrial Perspective
sources.usage_note: Sagan's energy-use interpretation of the Kardashev scale. The Type 0.7 value is a historical estimate, not a measured planetary parameter.
